validated_results.title: Urinary Trace Element Concentrations in Congolese Patients With Prostate Cancer: A Case-Control Study.
validated_results.reason: This human case-control study compares urinary selenium concentrations between prostate cancer patients and matched controls, providing a target-specific result for prostate cancer case status.

extraction.population: Men with prostate cancer and age-matched controls

sample_size.excerpt: The study included 94 PCa patients and 94 controls matched according to age and sociodemographic characteristics.
sample_size.location: abstract, methods; total_n derived from reported group counts 94 + 94 = 188

cases.excerpt: This case-control analytical study was conducted between April 5, 2018, and April 5, 2023, in Haut-Katanga Province, DRC. The study included 94 PCa patients and 94 controls matched according to age and sociodemographic characteristics.

p_value.excerpt: Compared with controls, PCa patients showed significantly higher urinary concentrations of arsenic, cadmium, cobalt, chromium, copper, manganese, selenium and zinc (p < 0.05), whereas aluminium concentrations were significantly lower.

design.excerpt: This case-control analytical study was conducted between April 5, 2018, and April 5, 2023

ethnicity.excerpt: were associated with PCa status in this Congolese population

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Urinary concentrations of 12 selected trace elements were measured using inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry.

extraction.direction_imputation_reason: Comparison direction was not explicit; the protocol assumes high versus low exposure.

parallel_r3_gate_reasons: JBI remains Fair after Claude R2
important quantitative evidence remains missing or invalid: ci_lower, ci_upper, effect_size, effect_type
